info.name: HRMS — Super Admin API
info.description:
Platform-level Super Admin panel APIs.

## Setup

1. Promote your users in SQL:
```sql
UPDATE users SET is_super_admin = TRUE WHERE email IN ('a@x.com', 'b@x.com');
```
2. Run **0. Auth → Login** — it saves `super_admin_token` automatically.
3. Set `company_id` / `target_company_id` from **3. Companies → List companies (lite)**.

## Model

Super Admin is a flag on the `users` row, not a company role. A super admin stays a normal Admin of their own company and additionally reads every company and can disable/enable them. Same login, same JWT.

## Conventions

- Analytics endpoints accept `?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`, defaulting to the last 30 days (the locations endpoint defaults to 7 days). The applied window is echoed back in `date_range`.
- Paginated responses carry `pagination { page, limit, total, totalPages, hasNextPage, hasPrevPage }`.
- Rates are percentages 0-100, pre-rounded. `punctuality_band` is one of `excellent` (>=95) | `good` (>=85) | `fair` (>=70) | `poor` (<70) | `no_data`.
- `present` = attendance status `checked-in`/`checked-out`; `punctual` = attendance_status `on-time`/`before-time`.
- Non-super-admins get 403 `NOT_SUPER_ADMIN`. The flag is re-checked against the DB on every request with a ~30s cache, so a raw SQL grant can take up to 30 seconds to take effect.

Example responses in this collection are illustrative, matching the exact field shapes the API returns.

variable.description: Company being inspected in the read endpoints
Company being disabled/enabled — must NOT be your own logged-in company
A record UUID, for the activity-log history endpoint
Used only by the lockout demonstration request

item.name: 0. Auth (prerequisite)
item.description:
Super Admin uses the SAME login endpoint as everyone else. There is no separate super admin login.

Promote a user to Super Admin directly in the database first:

```sql
UPDATE users SET is_super_admin = TRUE WHERE email IN ('a@x.com', 'b@x.com');
```

Then log in and copy `data.access_token` into the `super_admin_token` collection variable. Note: the backend caches the super-admin flag for ~30 seconds, so a fresh SQL grant can take up to half a minute to take effect.

request.description: Saves the returned access token into the `super_admin_token` collection variable automatically.
